title: Handling Missing Data in pandas & NumPy

scenes.say: Ever opened a dataset and seen a bunch of missing values? Let's talk about how to handle them the right way.

scenes.label: NaN
scenes.sub: Missing data in pandas shows up as NaN or None.
scenes.say: In pandas, missing values usually show up as NaN or None. You'll see these a lot in real-world data.
Use isnull to spot missing values. Fillna replaces them, like filling age with the average. Dropna lets you remove rows with missing salary.

rows.b: Fill or drop based on impact

scenes.say: I always check for patterns before changing anything. Sometimes it's better to fill, sometimes to drop. Handling this well keeps your analysis solid.

scenes.question: Should you always drop missing data?
scenes.right: No, dropping can lose valuable info. Inspect first, then fill or drop based on context.
scenes.say: Here's a trap: should you always drop missing data? Definitely not. Dropping everything can throw away useful info. Always inspect and decide what makes sense.
